html:
A Gothic people who entered the Roman Empire in 376, sacked Rome in 410 and went on to rule Spain until 711. The map shows them in 400 and 500; by 500 their kingdom spanned southwestern Gaul and most of Spain.

Fleeing the Huns, Gothic groups crossed the Danube in 376, and two years later they killed the emperor Valens at the Battle of Adrianople. Under Alaric I they marched through the Balkans and Italy and in 410 carried out the sack of Rome. In 418 Rome settled them in Aquitaine, with Toulouse as their capital. King Euric, who ruled from 466 to 484, broke free of Rome and conquered much of Spain.

In 507 the Franks under Clovis beat them at the Battle of Vouillé, and they lost almost all of Gaul. They moved their centre to Toledo, where the story goes on as the Visigothic Kingdom. Its king turned from Arian to Catholic Christianity in 587, and the kingdom fell to the Umayyad invasion of 711.
